items.title: ExxonMobil Awards Noble Drillship Contract at $375k/day in Guyana
items.summary: ExxonMobil awarded Noble Corporation a new drillship contract offshore Guyana at a day rate of $375,000. The contract supports continued development drilling at the Stabroek Block, one of the world's most prolific deepwater discoveries.

items.title: Seadrill Adds $260M Backlog with U.S. Gulf Drillship Awards
items.summary: Seadrill secured two drillship contract awards in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico. The West Neptune received a 365-day extension commencing September 2026, and the West Vela secured a 270-day contract starting August 2026, adding approximately $260 million in backlog.

items.title: Transocean Announces $425M Additional Backlog for Ultra-Deepwater Drillship
items.summary: Transocean secured $425 million in additional contract backlog for an ultra-deepwater drillship. The award reflects continued operator demand for high-specification 8th generation assets.

items.title: Transocean Wins $1B in Offshore Rig Contracts for Norway and Brazil
items.summary: Transocean announced contract awards totaling approximately $1.0 billion. The Transocean Barents was awarded a 1,095-day contract with Vår Energi in Norway at $450k/day (~$490M backlog). The Deepwater Orion secured a 1,095-day extension with Petrobras in Brazil (~$420M), and the Deepwater Aquila received a 365-day Petrobras extension (~$160M).

items.title: Transocean Deepwater Asgard Wins $158M Eastern Mediterranean Contract
items.summary: The Deepwater Asgard was awarded a five-well contract in the Eastern Mediterranean Sea with an undisclosed operator, adding approximately $158 million of backlog. The estimated 390-day campaign is expected to begin in Q4 2026.

items.title: Petrobras Awards Foresea $465M Drillship Contract for Mero Field
items.summary: Petrobras awarded Foresea a long-term contract to operate the ultra-deepwater drillship ODN I offshore Brazil. The 1,443-day campaign supports development activity in the Mero field in the Santos Basin, contributing approximately $465 million to backlog.

items.title: Transocean to Acquire Valaris for $5.8B, Creating World's Largest Offshore Driller
items.summary: Transocean announced an all-stock acquisition of Valaris valued at approximately $5.8 billion. The combined entity would operate 73 offshore rigs — 33 UDW drillships, 9 semisubmersibles, and 31 jackups — with a combined contract backlog of approximately $10 billion. Transaction expected to close in H2 2026, pending regulatory approvals.

items.title: Noble Completes $360M Sale of Five Jackups to Borr Drilling
items.summary: Noble Corporation completed the sale of five premium jack-up drilling rigs to Borr Drilling for approximately $360 million, including three Friede & Goldman JU-3000N and two Gusto MSC CJ50 design rigs. The transaction generated ~$210M cash and $150M in seller notes, expanding Borr's fleet to 29 jackups. Noble becomes a pureplay deepwater driller.

items.title: Seadrill Announces Multiple Contract Awards in Malaysia, Norway, and Brazil
items.summary: Seadrill secured three rig awards: West Capella contracted in Malaysia for ~440 days at $157M total value commencing Q2 2026; West Elara secured an accommodation contract with Equinor in Norway worth $78M starting Q3 2026; West Carina contract extended through April 2026 in Brazil.

items.title: Transocean FY2025: Revenue Up 13% to $3.97B, EBITDA Up 19% to $1.37B
items.summary: Transocean reported full-year 2025 contract drilling revenues of $3.965 billion (up 13% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $1.37 billion (up 19%). Q4 2025 revenue was $1.04 billion with a 37% EBITDA margin. Total backlog stood at approximately $6.1 billion. Record uptime of near 98% achieved across fleet.

items.title: Seadrill Q4 2025: Revenue $362M, EBITDA $88M — 2026 Guidance $1.4–1.45B
items.summary: Seadrill reported Q4 2025 revenue of $362 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $88 million (24.3% margin), with a net loss of $10 million. Full-year 2025 Adjusted EBITDA was $353 million. Backlog rose to $2.5 billion. 2026 guidance: revenue $1.40–1.45 billion, Adjusted EBITDA $350–400 million.

items.title: Valaris Q4 2025: Revenue $537M, Backlog $4.7B — Merger with Transocean Pending
items.summary: Valaris reported Q4 2025 revenue of $537 million and net income of $717 million including a tax benefit. Full-year 2025 revenue was $2.36 billion. Backlog expanded to $4.7 billion with ~97% of 2026 revenue midpoint already contracted. Valaris has cancelled future earnings calls due to the pending Transocean acquisition.

items.title: Borr Drilling Q4 2025: Revenue $259M, FY EBITDA $470M at Top of Guidance
items.summary: Borr Drilling reported Q4 2025 operating revenue of $259.4 million and full-year 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of $470.1 million, at the top of guidance. Q4 net loss was $1.0 million. Backlog stood at $1.2 billion. Fleet utilization was 85% for premium jackups.

items.title: Westwood: 2026 Offshore Rig Outlook Brightens After Mid-Cycle Pause
items.summary: Westwood Global Energy reported that offshore rig demand is strengthening with 355 rig-years of awarded demand for 2026 starts. The market outlook for 2027–2028 is particularly strong, with 42 unawarded tenders totaling ~67 combined rig-years. Drillship demand recovery is led by Brazil and the U.S. Gulf of Mexico.

items.title: Noble to Sell 6 Jackups to Become Pureplay Deepwater Driller
items.summary: Noble Corporation announced the sale of six jackup rigs — five to Borr Drilling and one to Ocean Oilfield — to become a pureplay deepwater drilling company. The strategic shift aligns Noble with the higher day rate UDW floater market and eliminates exposure to the more commoditized jackup segment.
